title: What Is the Minimum Salary Australia? A Guide to Hourly, Weekly and Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using the National Minimum Wage in Australia. Understand award rates, casual loading, super and tax for 2026–27.
salarySummary: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38‑hour week, giving an annual salary of $52,254.80 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on the minimum salary?

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Salary

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is understanding how they relate. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full‑time employees, we assume 38 ordinary hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Act. This gives a consistent baseline for comparing offers. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour works out to $1004.90 per week ($26.44 × 38) and $52,254.80 per year ($1004.90 × 52).

Many employers pay fortnightly, so you can also think of it as $2009.80 per fortnight (weekly pay × 2). This is a common pay cycle in Australia and helps with budgeting.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The **minimum salary Australia** is not a single figure for everyone. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that the National Minimum Wage applies only to employees who are not covered by an award or registered agreement. From 1 July 2026, that rate is $26.44 per hour or $1004.90 per week.

However, most employees are covered by an industry or occupation award. Awards set minimum pay rates that are often higher than the National Minimum Wage, plus they include penalty rates, allowances and overtime. For instance, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (SCHADS) has specific rates for different classifications. You can find the exact rates for your award on our [pay guides](/blog) page.

If you are covered by an enterprise agreement, check that document for your minimum pay. The Fair Work Commission approves these agreements, and they must not undercut the relevant award.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate. This loading is meant to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25).

When using our calculator, enter your base hourly rate **without** the casual loading. Then tick the casual loading checkbox, and the tool will add the 25% automatically. Never type a rate that already includes the loading, as that would double‑count it.

For award‑covered casuals, the loading may be built into the award rate or applied on top. Check your award’s pay guide for the correct method.

### Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your gross salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For someone on the National Minimum Wage, that means an extra $6,270.58 in super contributions annually, bringing the total employment cost to $58,525.38.

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool estimates your net income after these deductions, but it does not account for HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge or salary packaging.

### Using the Calculator

Our timesheet calculator lets you enter your hourly rate and choose whether you are casual. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. The formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances and no salary sacrifice.

For a more precise picture, compare your offer against the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics. As of May 2026, full‑time adult ordinary‑time earnings were $2083.70 per week, while total earnings (including part‑time) were $1579.20 per week. These figures give context to where your salary sits in the broader market.

Remember, the **minimum salary Australia** is a floor, not a target. Many awards and agreements pay well above it. Always check your award or agreement, and if you are unsure, contact the Fair Work Ombudsman for advice.

For more information, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) pages.
